ai.definition: A brain-computer interface that decodes intended speech from neural signals to enable communication for individuals who are unable to speak.
ai.howItWorks: Electrode arrays placed over the speech-motor cortex record neural activity, which is then translated by machine-learning models into words or text. This process often includes visual feedback through an on-screen avatar of a speaking head.
ai.problemSolved: Restores communication for individuals with paralysis, ALS, and other conditions that impair speech abilities.
ai.manufacturing: Involves the development and integration of electrode arrays, signal processing hardware, and machine-learning algorithms. Requires precise manufacturing techniques to ensure accurate recording and translation of neural signals.
ai.buildProcess: Includes the design and testing of electrode arrays, calibration of the system with individual users, training of machine-learning models on user-specific data, and integration of visual feedback systems.
ai.costDrivers: High costs associated with electrode array development, signal processing hardware, and specialized personnel for system calibration and maintenance. Significant investment in machine-learning model training and validation.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to transition from clinical trials to broader adoption as technology matures and more users gain access.
ai.regulation: Subject to regulatory approval processes, including clinical trial approvals, device certification, and post-market monitoring. Requires compliance with healthcare regulations governing medical devices and patient data privacy.
ai.risks: Technical risks related to electrode array performance, signal-to-noise ratio, and machine-learning model accuracy. Ethical concerns around user privacy, data security, and potential misuse of the technology.
ai.profitability: Potential for high profitability once the technology gains market acceptance and widespread use in clinical settings. However, initial costs and regulatory hurdles may limit short-term revenue generation.
ai.futureDevelopment: Expected to see advancements in electrode array design, miniaturization of hardware components, improvements in machine-learning algorithms, and integration with other BCI technologies for enhanced functionality.

glossary.def: Brain-computer interface, a system that enables direct communication between the brain and external devices.
A condition characterized by the loss of muscle function in a body part or limb.
Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, a progressive neurodegenerative disease that affects nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord, leading to muscle weakness and atrophy.

subsystems.name: Electrode array
subsystems.role: records neural activity from the speech-motor cortex.

subsystems.name: Signal acquisition and processing
subsystems.role: amplifies, digitises and filters raw neural signals.

subsystems.name: Neural decoder
subsystems.role: machine-learning model that translates neural patterns into intended speech.

subsystems.name: Output interface
subsystems.role: presents decoded speech as text, synthetic voice or an avatar.

subsystems.name: Surgical implantation system
subsystems.role: places electrodes safely in or on the brain.

subsystems.name: Training and calibration software
subsystems.role: lets the user practice and adapts the decoder to their unique signals.

buildSteps.title: Identify participants
buildSteps.detail: Clinical trials recruit people with severe paralysis or ALS who cannot speak but have intact speech-motor cortex.

buildSteps.title: Implant electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Neurosurgeons perform a craniotomy and place electrode arrays over or into the speech-motor cortex.

buildSteps.title: Connect to external hardware
buildSteps.detail: A percutaneous connector or wireless transmitter links the electrodes to a computer.

buildSteps.title: Record neural signals
buildSteps.detail: The system amplifies and digitises brain activity while the participant attempts to speak.

buildSteps.title: Train the decoder
buildSteps.detail: Machine-learning models are trained on the recorded signals paired with intended words or phonemes.

buildSteps.title: Decode speech in real time
buildSteps.detail: The trained model translates new neural activity into text, which can drive a synthetic voice and avatar.

buildSteps.title: Use and refine at home
buildSteps.detail: Participants use the system daily; engineers remotely update software and recalibrate as needed.

prerequisites.why: they provide the high-resolution neural signals needed for speech decoding.
neural signals must be amplified and digitised with minimal delay.
decoders work in trials but need larger vocabularies, faster speeds and robustness.
signals degrade over months or years, requiring recalibration or reimplantation.
regulators are developing pathways, but no speech BCI is approved for general use yet.

pathway.milestone: early clinical trials demonstrate text and voice output from attempted speech
pathway.unlocks: proof that the approach works in a few participants.

pathway.milestone: larger trials with wireless systems, bigger vocabularies and faster decoding
pathway.unlocks: reliable daily use for a wider group of patients.

pathway.milestone: regulatory approval for clinical use as a medical device

pathway.unlocks: routine use and potential for other applications.
